newsitem.title: KENYA: Kuehne plans Tanzanian flower charters.
newsitem.headline: Kuehne plans Tanzanian flower charters.

text.p: Swiss freight forwarder Kuehne & Nagel has opened a representative office in Tanzania's northern town of Arusha and expects to launch charter cargo flights from there later this year, a company official said on Friday.

Myles Hechle, operations manager for Airlink, an 85 percent-owned subsidiary of the Swiss company in Kenya, said Tanzania's rapidly growing flower industry was becoming increasingly interesting for the air cargo industry.

"Tanzania is the place everyone is getting excited about now. I think the potential is huge there. At the moment growers are sending huge truck loads of flowers to Nairobi and are just waiting for someone to start charters from Kilimanjaro Airport."
"The registered Kuehne & Nagel office is up and running and ready to go. The charters will start by October or November if everything works out as planned," Hechle told Reuters.
Kuehne & Nagel plans to start a scheduled cargo service by chartering smaller planes than the 747s used from Nairobi.
Tanzania's horticulture industry, and in particular exports of cut flowers to European destinations, has doubled many times over the past two years.

Located in the northern areas surrounding Mount Kilimanjaro between the towns of Arusha and Moshi, Tanzania's flower industry has some 140 hectares under cultivation and is already the fifth-biggest in Africa.
Hechle said Kuehne & Nagel initially would be looking at operating three direct charters a week to Amsterdam and Frankfurt from Kilimanjaro International Airport.

"Three times a week would be ideal, with flowers to both Amsterdam and Frankfurt. Our strength has been flowers and Tanzania is becoming a big market, the potential in the Arusha and Kilimanjaro area is huge.

"It will take some time to set up the charters because it (Tanzania) hasn't had that service yet, but I think in one year from now you will see three or four weekly charters with flowers from Kilimanjaro," Hechle said. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
